New: a Board that groups every session and pull request by what needs you, each session's pull request on its row, a Mac that stays awake while an agent works, a check of each deploy after a push, and Cursor tokens and cost. After upgrading, sign in to Datadog once more if you use Prod.

What's new

- Board: the Board button in the Agents header opens one view with four groups: Needs you, Working, In review and Ready to merge. A session on a pull request is one card showing both, under the more urgent of the two. Idle sessions with no pull request fold into one collapsed line. Pending approvals stay pinned above any open panel, so they are never hidden. The Board makes no requests of its own.
- Pull requests on session rows: a session in a git folder whose branch is the source of one of your Bitbucket pull requests shows a line with the PR number and its state: build failed, merge conflict, can't merge, new comments, approved, changes requested, draft or build running. Click opens the PR.
- Send to agent: hands the agent a short brief of what to fix (the failed step and the end of its log, the new comments, or the conflict). A running Claude Code turn gets it as a note at its next step; any other session gets it on the clipboard. Logs and comments are fetched only when you click, and secrets in them are masked.
- Pull request notifications: a notification when a pull request is merged or declined (with who did it), and when it is ready to merge (once per commit). Each has a checkbox in Setup.
- Mac stays awake: while any session works, the Mac does not go to sleep on its own, and it stays awake for 2 minutes after the last one stops. Two switches in Setup → Effects turn it off, one of them for battery only (it still lets go below 20%).
- Steadier session list: a session is dropped only once its process is really gone, so a row no longer disappears for a moment while the agent is still running.
- Prod after a push: for 20 minutes after a push from a repo linked in builds.json "services", the Prod card compares the new version with the previous one: error rate, p95 and requests per minute, plus error types seen only on the new version. When the version does not change, it compares the time since the push with the same stretch before it.
- Prod deploys and Watchdog: the Prod card lists recent deploys (prod and production count as one) and Datadog Watchdog stories, with a chip when one is active. "hiddenServices" in builds.json (default leads*) keeps a service out of Prod entirely: monitors, incidents, Watchdog and deploys.
- Cursor usage: tokens and cost for Cursor now come from your Cursor account, and show as Cursor in the usage panel. AI Notch reads Cursor's sign-in on your Mac and pulls usage events from cursor.com; the token stays in memory and goes only to cursor.com. The cost is Cursor's own plan-usage charge, not money billed on Business plans. An incomplete history is flagged in the panel.
- Other agents: OpenCode installed from npm (its program is opencode.exe) is now found.

After upgrading

- The first launch rebuilds your usage history, which takes about 35 seconds. Cursor history then loads for a few minutes, and new Cursor usage is read at most once a minute.
- Prod: sign in to Datadog once more. Sign-in now also asks for apm_read and events_read, which the deploy checks and Watchdog need.
- Pull request features need Bitbucket set up as before. Setup has the new notification checkboxes.

Known limits

- Cursor cost is Cursor's own charge for plan usage. On Business plans it is not what you are billed.
- Prod requests stay within 144 an hour, so deploy checks can lag a little behind Datadog.

Install or upgrade:

    brew install --cask ankeshshankar/tap/ai-notch
    brew upgrade --cask ai-notch

First open: the app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so macOS blocks it once. Open AI Notch, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. If Set Up then reports the helper is blocked, run the command it shows:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AINotch.app

Requires macOS 15 or later.
